A SEPARATE registration on the same gate as controls/codex-skill-sync-remap and controls/codex-skill-sync-over-bundle (row 33's first controls, issue #1408 ruling: per-axis, since all three fire on unrelated signals). This one covers bullet 2 only: the network-helper advisory detector's false positives.

WHAT 'FINDING' MEANS HERE: a single shared predicate for both cases - `calls_network()` answering False on the fixture. For the bad case (a known false-positive shape) that means the fix correctly suppressed it; for the good case (a real network call) False would mean the fix over-corrected into blindness, so that case's own `expect: GOOD` catches a broken fix that swings too far the other way, not just one that does nothing.

WHY THE ADAPTER CALLS `calls_network()` DIRECTLY rather than driving the full `generate_skill()` pipeline: the detector operates on BUNDLED SCRIPT CONTENT (the `files` dict `generate_skill` assembles from whatever `find_bundled_scripts`/`find_bundled_libs` resolve against the real checkout's SCRIPTS_ROOT), never on a command document's body directly - the body only decides WHICH scripts get bundled. Routing a fixture through the whole pipeline would need a fixture script actually present under `scripts/` to be discovered, which is a bigger and less direct dependency than calling the one function this axis is actually about.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES (issue #1408, Nit Store #864, found by the #1359 counter-model review and deferred then): an argv-shaped list inside a Python docstring (`"""...run(["gh", "issue", "list"])..."""`) no longer stamps the Network adaptation bullet on a skill whose helpers make no real call - ast.parse represents a docstring as ONE Constant node, which can never contain a nested List node, so the AST walk simply does not generate the shape the old regex matched. The paired good case is the ruling's own explicit ask: a REAL `subprocess.run(["gh", "issue", "list"])` call must still be flagged - proving the fix narrows the detector rather than disabling it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Nothing about the shell-side fix (the quoted-string false positive, or the command-substitution-inside-a-double-quote case the fix's own build surfaced as a near-regression) - both are pytest-covered in tests/test_codex_skill_sync.py (test_calls_network_ignores_a_mention, test_calls_network_flags_a_substitution_inside_a_double_quote), not duplicated here since a control's job is proving the Python-side fix is not blind on a real input, not re-walking every shape a unit test suite already owns. Nothing about bullets 3/4, which have their own registrations.
